_comment: Interactive Speaking topics. Each topic has 4 questions in order; each question has an easier and a harder version. The app switches version based on how well the previous answer went, like the adaptive real test.

questions.easy: Where are you from? Tell me a little about your hometown.
questions.hard: Tell me about the place where you grew up and what makes it different from other places.

questions.easy: What do people usually do there in their free time?
questions.hard: How do people in your hometown usually spend their free time, and has that changed in recent years?

questions.easy: Do you like living there? Why or why not?
questions.hard: What are the main advantages and disadvantages of living in your hometown?

questions.easy: What would you change about your hometown?
questions.hard: If you were the mayor of your hometown, what is one change you would make, and why would it matter?

questions.easy: What do you study, or what would you like to study?
questions.hard: Tell me about the subject you study or want to study, and why you chose it.

questions.easy: Where do you like to study? Why?
questions.hard: Describe the environment where you study best, and explain why it works for you.

questions.easy: Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?
questions.hard: Some people say studying in groups is more effective than studying alone. What is your view?

questions.easy: What is the most difficult part of studying for you?
questions.hard: What is the biggest challenge students face today, and how could schools help them with it?

questions.easy: How often do you use your phone? What do you use it for?
questions.hard: Describe how technology fits into your daily routine, from morning to night.

questions.easy: What is your favorite app? Why do you like it?
questions.hard: Tell me about a piece of technology that has changed the way you live or work.

questions.easy: Do you think people use their phones too much?
questions.hard: Some people believe smartphones are making us less social. Do you agree or disagree, and why?

questions.easy: What new technology would you like to have in the future?
questions.hard: How do you think artificial intelligence will change education or work in the next ten years?

questions.easy: What is your favorite food? Why do you like it?
questions.hard: Tell me about a dish that is important to you or your family, and why it matters.

questions.easy: Do you like cooking? What can you cook?
questions.hard: How did you learn to cook, or why have you not learned yet?

questions.easy: Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
questions.hard: What are the advantages and disadvantages of eating out compared to cooking at home?

questions.easy: Do you think people eat healthy food today?
questions.hard: Whose responsibility is it to make sure people eat healthily: individuals, families, or governments?

questions.easy: Do you like to travel? Where have you been?
questions.hard: Tell me about the most interesting place you have ever visited.

questions.easy: What do you like to do when you visit a new place?
questions.hard: When you visit a new place, how do you prefer to explore it, and why?

questions.easy: Do you prefer to travel alone or with friends?
questions.hard: What can people learn from travelling that they cannot learn at home?

questions.easy: Where would you like to travel in the future?
questions.hard: Some people say tourism harms the places people visit. What do you think, and what could be done about it?

questions.easy: What job do you have, or what job would you like to have?
questions.hard: Tell me about the career you are hoping to build and how you became interested in it.

questions.easy: What makes a job a good job?
questions.hard: Which matters more when choosing a job: the salary or job satisfaction? Explain your view.

questions.easy: Would you like to work from home? Why?
questions.hard: How has the way people work changed in recent years, and is this change positive?

questions.easy: What skills are important for your future job?
questions.hard: What skills do you think young people need most to succeed in tomorrow's job market?

questions.easy: What do you like to do in your free time?
questions.hard: Tell me about a hobby that you are passionate about and how you got started.

questions.easy: Do you prefer to spend free time indoors or outdoors?
questions.hard: How do you balance your free time with your responsibilities?

questions.easy: Did you have the same hobbies when you were a child?
questions.hard: How have your interests changed since you were a child, and why do you think that happened?

questions.easy: Is there a new hobby you want to try?
questions.hard: Do you think hobbies are important for people's mental health? Why or why not?

questions.easy: Do you think about the environment in your daily life?
questions.hard: What do you personally do to reduce your impact on the environment?

questions.easy: Is there a lot of pollution where you live?
questions.hard: What is the most serious environmental problem in your country, and what causes it?

questions.easy: Do you recycle? Why or why not?
questions.hard: Should governments force people to recycle, or should it be a personal choice?

questions.easy: What can young people do to help the planet?
questions.hard: Are individual actions enough to solve climate change, or do we need bigger changes? Explain.

questions.easy: Tell me about your family.
questions.hard: Tell me about a family member who has influenced you, and how.

questions.easy: What do you like to do with your friends?
questions.hard: What qualities do you think make someone a good friend?

questions.easy: Do you prefer having many friends or a few close friends?
questions.hard: Is it easier or harder to make friends as an adult than as a child? Why?

questions.easy: How do you keep in touch with friends who live far away?
questions.hard: How has social media changed friendships, for better or for worse?

questions.easy: What kind of music do you like?
questions.hard: Tell me about a song, book, or film that means something special to you.

questions.easy: Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema?
questions.hard: How has the way people watch films and series changed in the last few years?

questions.easy: Do you like reading? What do you read?
questions.hard: Do you think reading books is still important now that we have so much video content? Why?

questions.easy: Would you like to learn to play an instrument?
questions.hard: Should music and art be as important as maths and science in schools? Explain your opinion.
